messages:
deploy-bot: ALERT: canary v6.1.0 increased 5xx rate on streaming route 'chat-us' (+4.2% over baseline). Autorevert scheduled in 3m. metrics: https://telemetry/redwood/v6.1.0
harpreet: Noticed. Looks like errors originate from a small subset of pods in us-east-1c. Can we pause autorevert while we check logs?
mike: Oncall. If it's shard-local, prefer a targeted route pin rather than full revert to avoid rolling back unrelated routes. Can someone confirm affected shard?
ivy: I can tail logs: ```bash
kubectl -n prod logs -l app=chat-us,pod=chat-us-abc --since=10m | grep -i "rpc:error" -n | tail -n 50
```
carla: I'll prepare a short rollback note for customers if we widen it. @cs-team FYI.
ops-bot: Autorevert in 180s. Operator override required to suppress.
harpreet: I'll take override. Proposal: suppress autorevert for 20m, run route-pin for chat-us to v6.0.9, drain bad pods, and monitor for 15m. If other regions show similar errors, escalate to full revert.
mike: Command to run: ```bash
rls route-pin --env canary --route chat-us --to v6.0.9 --reason "localized 5xx spike"
```
ops-bot: Operator override request from harpreet accepted. Suppressing autorevert for 20m.
ops-bot: Executing: rls route-pin --env canary --route chat-us --to v6.0.9
ops-bot: SUCCESS: route chat-us pinned to v6.0.9. Traffic rebalanced.
ivy: After pinning, 5xx rate dropped on chat-us pods. Initial traces show an Nginx upstream timeout tied to a new keepalive config. Logging an example trace to ticket RL-7015.
carla: Posted customer note: "We rerouted a small subset of traffic to a prior version due to increased errors; investigating root cause. No customer data exposure. We'll update within 30 minutes." Posted to #customer-notify.
mike: Leaving pin in place for 30m. Filing postmortem and linking the keepalive config diff. If stable, we can unpin and re-deploy with config reverted.
harpreet: Manual intervention complete: autorevert suppressed, targeted route pin applied, CS notified, postmortem filed. Thanks folks :thumbsup:
